slides.label: Cold Open
slides.text: Shift change. A factory floor, afternoon bleeding into evening. Dave pulls his lock off the disconnect and heads for the exit — outgoing crew, done for the day.

slides.label: The Gap
slides.boxText: For the next four minutes, this machine is unprotected.
slides.body: The outgoing crew pulled their locks. The incoming crew hasn't applied theirs yet. In that gap, anyone could start this machine.

slides.heading:
New lock on.
Then old lock off.
slides.body: The incoming worker's lock goes on while the outgoing worker's lock is still there. At no point is the hasp empty. At no point is the machine unprotected.

slides.label: Group Lockout
slides.boxText: One worker, one machine, one lock — the principle scales.
slides.body: A group coordinator manages the process without replacing individual locks. Each worker applies their own. The machine can't restart until the last lock is off.

slides.heading:
One lock on the machine.
The key goes in a box.
Everyone locks the box.
slides.body: The machine can't restart until the lockbox opens. The lockbox can't open until every worker removes their lock. Same protection. Different geometry.

items.text: Inspect. Make sure the work is actually finished.
Clean up. Parts, rags, work aids back where they belong.
Replace guards. Every guard goes back before startup.
Check controls. Everything in neutral or its safest position.
Check for personnel. A headcount, not a glance.
Notify — devices removed. Before the machine restarts.
Notify — ready for use. After the job is actually done.

slides.heading:
Notice one:
the locks are off.
slides.body: Notify affected employees that the lockout devices have been removed. This happens before the machine restarts, not after — the standard is specific about the window.

source.anchor: After lockout or tagout devices have been removed and before a machine or equipment is started, affected employees shall be notified that the lockout or tagout device(s) have been removed.

slides.label: Re-energize
slides.boxText: Only after that notice goes out.
slides.body: Follow the documented startup sequence for this equipment — not just the reverse of shutdown.

slides.heading:
Notice two:
the job is done.
slides.body: Notify affected employees that the servicing is complete and the machine is ready for use. A separate notice, after the machine is running.

source.citation: 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(9); Appendix A, Restoring Equipment to Service, step (5)
source.anchor: (c)(9): "Affected employees shall be notified by the employer or authorized employee of the application and removal of lockout devices or tagout devices. Notification shall be given before the controls are applied, and after they are removed from the machine or equipment." / Appendix A step (5): "Notify affected employees that the servicing or maintenance is completed and the machine or equipment is ready for use."

options.title: Lock removed in your absence
options.desc: You're notified, before you return to any equipment.

slides.label: When They're Not Available
slides.text: A disconnect with a single lock. Shift's over. Dave's lock. Dave's gone. Not answering his phone.

slides.label: Not a Coworker's Call
slides.boxText: Only under the employer's direction, through a procedure documented in advance.
slides.body: Nobody improvises this in the moment. Verify the employee is absent — not in the building, not on break. Make reasonable efforts to contact them, and document the attempts. Inform them before they return — before they approach any equipment.

source.anchor: Exception to paragraph (e)(3): When the authorized employee who applied the lockout or tagout device is not available to remove it, that device may be removed under the direction of the employer, provided that specific procedures and training for such removal have been developed, documented and incorporated into the employer's energy control program.

slides.heading:
The lock removal isn't
complete until they know.
slides.body: A worker returning to a machine they think is locked out, reaching in confident — that's the alternative this requirement prevents.

slides.heading:
Written into the standard,
not made up to save time.
slides.body: Places where the standard draws its own boundaries. Learn them as boundaries, not shortcuts.

slides.label: Cord-and-Plug Equipment
slides.boxText: Unplugged AND under your exclusive control — both, not one.
slides.body: A bench grinder. A portable drill. If the plug stays under your exclusive control — your hand, your pocket, not set down anywhere someone else could reach it — this standard doesn't require lockout on it.

source.anchor: Work on cord and plug connected electric equipment for which exposure to the hazards of unexpected energization or start up of the equipment is controlled by the unplugging of the equipment from the energy source and by the plug being under the exclusive control of the employee performing the servicing or maintenance.

slides.heading:
Minor servicing —
read the fence twice.
slides.body: A narrow exception for minor tool changes and adjustments — but only during normal production, only if the work is routine and repetitive and integral to how the equipment runs, and only if you're using an alternative measure that actually protects you. Every condition has to hold. Every time.

source.anchor: Exception to paragraph (a)(2)(ii): Minor tool changes and adjustments, and other minor servicing activities, which take place during normal production operations, are not covered by this standard if they are routine, repetitive, and integral to the use of the equipment for production, provided that the work is performed using alternative measures which provide effective protection (See subpart O of this part).

slides.heading:
"Clearing a jam"
is the classic misuse.
slides.body: If your alternative measure isn't actually providing effective protection, you don't have an exception. You have an unprotected worker near a hazard.

slides.label: Testing / Positioning
slides.boxText: An exact sequence, in order — not an ad-hoc override.
slides.body: Clear tools and personnel. Remove LOTO devices. Energize, test or position. De-energize, reapply LOTO. Same discipline as the six steps.

source.anchor: In situations in which lockout or tagout devices must be temporarily removed from the energy isolating device and the machine or equipment energized to test or position the machine, equipment or component thereof, the following sequence of actions shall be followed:

slides.label: Three Roles — 29 CFR 1910.147(b)
slides.body: Each role carries different responsibilities, different training, different obligations.

source.anchor: Affected employee.   An employee whose job requires him/her to operate or use a machine or equipment on which servicing or maintenance is being performed under lockout or tagout, or whose job requires him/her to work in an area in which such servicing or maintenance is being performed. / Authorized employee.   A person who locks out or tags out machines or equipment in order to perform servicing or maintenance on that machine or equipment.

slides.heading:
One performs
the lockout.
One never restarts it.
slides.body: Authorized employees are trained on every energy source, every isolation point — they apply the locks, they verify the isolation. Affected employees don't perform the lockout, but their work depends on it — an operator whose line is shut down for maintenance. Their job: never attempt to restart locked-out equipment. Ever.

slides.label: Other Employees
slides.body: Lockout exists. Locked-out equipment is off-limits. Attempting to start it can kill the person inside.

source.anchor: (A) Each authorized employee shall receive training in the recognition of applicable hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of the energy available in the workplace, and the methods and means necessary for energy isolation and control. / (B) Each affected employee shall be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure. / (C) All other employees whose work operations are or may be in an area where energy control procedures may be utilized, shall be instructed about the procedure, and about the prohibition relating to attempts to restart or reenergize machines or equipment which are locked out or tagged out.

slides.heading:
"Qualified person"
isn't a fourth role.
slides.body: It's a real OSHA term — just not from this standard. It means trained to work on or near exposed energized electrical parts. A qualified person might also be an authorized employee on a lockout — those aren't mutually exclusive. It's just a different question.

source.anchor: Qualified person.   One who has received training in and has demonstrated skills and knowledge in the construction and operation of electric equipment and installations and the hazards involved.

slides.heading:
Your role can change
with your duties.
slides.body: An affected employee becomes an authorized employee the moment their duties include performing servicing or maintenance. The roles aren't fixed identities — they're tied to what you're doing right now.

source.anchor: An affected employee becomes an authorized employee when that employee's duties include performing servicing or maintenance covered under this section.

slides.label: The Thesis
slides.boxText: Every piece of paper exists because someone was hurt by its absence.
slides.body: The procedure form is the map. The training certification is proof you were taught this. The inspection certification is proof someone verified it.

slides.label: The System Checks Itself
slides.body: Outside contractors: the on-site and outside employer inform each other of their procedures — a conversation, not a document either side signs and files. And once a year, an authorized employee who isn't involved in a given procedure watches another authorized employee perform it.

source.anchor: Whenever outside servicing personnel are to be engaged in activities covered by the scope and application of this standard, the on-site employer and the outside employer shall inform each other of their respective lockout or tagout procedures.

slides.label: Back to Shift Change
slides.text: The same factory floor. Shift change. But now the handoff is different.

slides.label: Scene
slides.text: The incoming worker inside the machine. Working steadily. The lock visible in the background. Protection in place.

slides.heading:
The difference is
thirty seconds
and a padlock.
slides.body: The procedure is simple. The edge cases are manageable. The paperwork has a purpose. The principle never changes — it just adapts.

slides.heading:
Six sources.
Six steps.
Three roles.
slides.body: Six named energy sources, each with its own stored-energy shadow. Six steps that turn off into safe. Three roles, each with a job. And protocols for when the simple case gets complicated.

slides.heading: Module 3 — Key Concepts
items: Restoring equipment ends with two notices: locks removed before restart, job done after
Group lockout and the lockbox method: one person, one lock, at any scale
Shift changes: new lock on before old lock off closes the gap
Cord-and-plug, minor servicing, testing/positioning: narrow fenced exceptions, not shortcuts
Lock removed in your absence: verify, attempt contact, notify you before you return
Authorized employees perform the lockout; affected employees never attempt to restart it
"Qualified person" is a real term — from electrical safety, not this standard
Paperwork and the annual review are evidence the system worked and checks itself

quiz.question: During a shift change on a machine that's under lockout, the correct procedure is:
options: The outgoing crew removes their locks, then the incoming crew applies theirs
The incoming crew applies their locks while the outgoing crew's locks are still in place, then the outgoing crew removes theirs
The outgoing crew leaves their locks for the incoming crew to use
A supervisor holds a master lock during the transition

quiz.question: A worker's lock is on a machine, but they've left the facility without removing it. The correct response is:
options: Cut the lock immediately — production is delayed
Leave the lock in place indefinitely until the worker returns

Verify the worker is absent, attempt to contact them, remove the lock following the employer's documented procedure for an unavailable employee, and ensure the worker is notified before returning to work
Have another authorized employee remove the lock since they have the same training

quiz.question: A machine has room for only one lock on its energy isolation point, but four workers need to service it. The correct approach is:
options: The team lead places the single lock and holds the key for the group
Workers take turns — one works while the others wait, each applying their lock for their turn
The coordinator locks the machine, places the key in a lockbox, and each worker places their own lock on the lockbox
One lock is sufficient as long as everyone agrees not to remove it

quiz.question: An operator's production line is shut down because maintenance is performing lockout/tagout on a connected machine. The operator is classified as:
options: An authorized employee, because they operate the equipment
An affected employee, whose primary responsibility is to never attempt to restart locked-out equipment
A qualified person, since this standard uses that term for anyone experienced with the equipment
An other employee, because they aren't involved in the maintenance

source.anchor: Qualified person.   One who has received training in and has demonstrated skills and knowledge in the construction and operation of electric equipment and installations and the hazards involved.
